newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Ladbroke poised to go up to 260p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Ladbroke poised to go up to 260p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
+ A minimum target for Ladbroke shares is 260p once resistance at 245p has been broken, technical analysts said, adding that longer-term the shares could go on to 340p.

+ The stock's consolidation phase since the start of the year has enabled its 25- and 200-day moving averages to converge but the recent share price strength should now pull them apart to confirm the bull trend.
A long-term uptrend in shares of hotels and leisure company Ladbroke Group Plc should enable them to overcome resistance at 245p and head for at least 260p, technical analysts said.
Since the start of the year the stock has drifted down a little but managed to spike higher on occasion although these spikes have always met resistance at 245p.

"A brief consolidation has taken place establishing support at 220p," said Robin Griffiths, technical analyst at HSBC James Capel. "The minimum target is the old high of 260p but the next quantum level is 340p."
By 0945 GMT, Ladbroke shares were unchanged at 242p.

According to Griffiths, share prices in general move in discrete or quantum steps of 25 percent from significant highs or lows. Ladbroke has doubled from a low of 125p in November 1995 so that a further 25 percent would take them to 280p with an intermediate stop at 260p.

This quantum theory has held up well in the past for Ladbroke because the shares consolidated around the 50- and 75-percent steps -- or 188p to 220p -- between the spring and autumn of 1996 as the long-term trend developed.
"This stock is in a prime uptrend -- and has been since January 1995," said Griffiths. "The rise to date has been consolidated and another surge seems to be starting."
Following the share price as it has marched higher since 1995 has been the stock's 200-day moving average which has also been a support line whenever the shares have experienced bouts of weakness.
Divergence between Ladbroke's 25- and 200-day moving averages has started to widen as the near-term average pulls away and this reflects a buoyant share price, analysts said.
